candidate.educational_objective: Apply contemporary nurse-leader competencies by combining psychological safety, staff development/engagement, communication, and shared quality-and-safety improvement goals.

options.A: Set all goals alone, discourage staff input, and use corrective discipline as the main method for obtaining compliance with unit expectations.
options.B: Avoid setting a shared direction and let each staff member define separate priorities because leader involvement reduces professional autonomy and teamwork goals.
options.C: Create psychological safety and effective communication, involve staff in improvement work, develop team members, and build a shared direction tied to quality and safety goals.
options.D: Focus mainly on short-term rewards for task completion without mentoring, shared purpose, learning, or staff participation in improving care.

candidate.rationale: The 2026 AONL Nurse Leader Core Competencies include Effective Communication, Relationship Management, Psychological Safety, and Interprofessional Collaboration, along with Quality, Safety and Improvement Science and Workforce Leadership and Optimization. A manager who builds psychological safety, develops staff, and engages the team around shared quality and safety goals is therefore aligned with the current framework.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current AONL competencies explicitly connect nurse leadership with communication, psychological safety, collaboration, quality/safety improvement, and workforce leadership.
candidate.source_locator: Core Competency Domains and Subdomains: Communication and Relational Leadership (Effective Communication, Relationship Management, Psychological Safety, Interprofessional Collaboration); Knowledge of the Health Care Environment (Quality, Safety and Improvement Science); Business Skills and Principles (Workforce Leadership and Optimization).

candidate.stem: A nurse manager wants to improve a unit with low morale and inconsistent quality-improvement participation. Which leadership behavior best aligns with current nurse-leader competencies?
